A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bernoulli-mask policy-gradient pruning work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning experiments, perplexity and zero-shot results, resource measurements, ablations and ten-run statistics.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds gradient-estimator comparisons, additional benchmarks, calibration-data analyses and generated examples.

M1.justification: The Bernoulli masks, projected policy-gradient updates, moving-average baseline, deterministic evaluation masks and initialization strategies remain unchanged. Random-progressive pruning already appears in v2. Gumbel Softmax is newly evaluated as a comparison variant.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix A.10 adds LAMBADA, RACE and BoolQ zero-shot evaluation and five-shot MMLU, substantially broadening task coverage beyond v2's five zero-shot tasks. The original model families and C4, WikiText2 and Alpaca coverage remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds Gumbel Softmax comparisons in Section 5.2, SLEB to layer-pruning and initialization comparisons in Tables A7 and A16, and a separate weight-updating FLAP/search-llm comparison in Table A10. Dense-model reference rows are also added. The original width-pruning comparator set remains.

E3.justification: New protocols include 10–20% pruning evaluations, five-shot MMLU, WikiText2 calibration and 2048-token evaluation for the weight-update comparison, and calibration sample/sequence-length sweeps with fixed optimization steps. Appendix A.19 also adds comparisons using identical 128-by-2048-token calibration data. The original main C4-to-WikiText2, 128-token protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 newly tests the performance/resource tradeoff between policy gradient and Gumbel Softmax. Appendix A.19 adds calibration-size sensitivity tests and common-calibration controls; Appendix A.13 adds generation case studies. Existing initialization, moving-average, global/local pruning and module-sparsity analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v3 specifies five replicates with means and standard deviations for the new calibration ablations in Appendix A.19. The original ten-trial uncertainty study is unchanged in v2 Appendix A.9 and v3 Appendix A.14; its run count was not reduced or increased.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark, comparator, resource, calibration and generation results. Original Table 1 pruned-model scores remain unchanged, but reported LLaMA-3-8B perplexity at 50% layer pruning changes from 325.37 in v2 Table 2 to 295.39 in v3 Table A7. LLaMA-2-7B pruning memory changes from 18.2–19.5 to 17.2–17.4 GB in the corresponding appendix tables. Results from newly introduced protocols are additional evidence, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, policy-gradient derivation, projection theorem, reinforcement-learning formulation and control-variate analysis remain substantively unchanged. Shortened loss notation and the corrected equation cross-reference in Appendix A.1 do not alter mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the headline contribution framing toward width pruning, explicitly calling channels and heads its main concern and dropping the separate flexibility contribution from the abstract, introduction and conclusion. Layer-pruning support and evaluation remain. The central forward-only, global/heterogeneous pruning claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds a tentative variance explanation for the 50% pruning deficit against Gumbel Softmax, develops applicability when memory accommodates only unpruned-model inference, and explains why fewer calibration samples need not reduce runtime under fixed steps. It also interprets generated examples as evidence of knowledge retention. Existing domain-dependence limitations and module-importance interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the future code-release promise with stated code availability and a repository link. It additionally documents the fixed-step/variable-epoch rule for calibration ablations, shared calibration settings and generation-prompt provenance. Existing SGD, LoRA and hardware disclosures are largely retained; repository availability is only established as a statement in the PDF.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly connects the framework to NAS/DARTS. Figure 1 substantially updates the research landscape, including SparseLLM and MaskLLM in categories marked unavailable in v2, alongside newer pruning works such as SLEB and search-llm. Several older general-pruning references are removed; publication updates to retained citations are separate bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodological explanations undergo extensive condensation and rewriting. Layer-pruning results and module-sparsity analysis move to appendices; conclusion and limitations become separate sections, and ethical considerations and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the single-column layout with two columns, restructures table placement and captions, adds several experimental displays and converts the appendix guide into a table. The two existing module-sparsity plots are redrawn and combined in Figure A2; the global/local plot is relabeled, and layer-pruning tables move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the central efficiency/accuracy tradeoff through the direct Gumbel Softmax comparison absent in v2. Calibration sensitivity tests and matched-data comparisons address important gaps in robustness and comparison fairness, while dense references make pruning losses easier to assess. These gains outweigh limited new reporting defects: Appendix A.5 miscalculates resource-saving percentages, and the new 1.56-hour runtime conflicts with the retained 1.76-hour statement in A.6.
